note: Placement: for this record Prunella is the accentor genus (dunnock Prunella modularis, alpine accentor P. collaris), Prunellidae (Passeriformes); the queue files it under Lamiaceae (self-heal and mints), so the harvest's family review "Lamiaceae photoreceptor review" (284 hits) searched the plant family and is discarded, not listed in queries; the harvest's plant-side queries "Prunella olfaction chemoreception" and "Prunella nocturnal diurnal activity" are listed because they ran. The harvest's candidates are herbal-medicine papers on Prunella vulgaris (myopia, glaucoma, macular degeneration), machine-vision reviews, songbird migration papers that name no eye measurement, and plant-pigment papers. Web: "Prunella visual acuity" returned human acuity pages and patents; "dunnock visual acuity" returned the bird acuity compilation (Ecological and morphological correlates of visual acuity in birds), Wikipedia and a mammal retina preprint; "Prunella visual field" returned human perimetry pages; "dunnock visual field" returned Wikipedia, photo sites and one Frontiers in Neuroscience PDF (10.3389/fnins.2018.00016) with no title shown, which is a lead on the wanted list, so binocular_deg and fov_h_deg are not in this genus's record; "Prunella flicker fusion" and "dunnock flicker fusion" returned human flicker pages, patents, a hen flicker-fusion method paper, one Springer item with no title (10.1007/BF02160841, not judged) and a Newcastle record (eprint3.ncl.ac.uk/232781) with no title; "Prunella spectral sensitivity" and "dunnock spectral sensitivity" returned damselfly, dung-beetle, fish and Drosophila papers, a physicsworld piece on cuckoo egg forgeries seen through bird vision, an AGRIS record and an RVC repository record with no title shown, and no dunnock measurement. "Prunellidae vision review" returned an overview of the penguin visual system, a mammalian retina preprint, the book How Animals See the World, the Wikipedia article on bird vision and family pages on the accentors. Main holds no Prunella animal row for these traits (its Prunella rows are plant light responses). WebSearch returned result titles and links only, so web results were judged by title.

note: Placement: Morus is the gannet genus (northern gannet M. bassanus, Australasian gannet M. serrator), Sulidae (Suliformes); the queue files it under Moraceae (mulberry). The harvest holds no entry for Morus (screen_candidates.py: "not in the harvest"), so no harvest query ran and none is listed; no harvest family review exists to discard. The searches are the web pairs and the family step "Sulidae vision review". Web: "Morus visual acuity" returned human acuity pages, patents, the bird acuity compilation (Ecological and morphological correlates of visual acuity in birds), a Smithsonian repository file and a Massey University thesis record; "northern gannet visual acuity" returned a fact sheet, two Massey University records (mro.massey.ac.nz handle 10179/4260 and an item page), a paper titled "Visual accommodation and active pursuit of prey underwater in a plunge-diving bird: The Australasian gannet" (University of Haifa record), PMC3441088 and species pages; these are leads on the wanted list, so acuity_cpd and interreceptor_deg are not in this record. "Morus visual field" returned human perimetry pages; "northern gannet visual field" returned species pages, photo pages and a Pennsylvania bird-records PDF, with no visual-field measurement. "Morus flicker fusion" returned human flicker pages, a budgerigar flicker-fusion revisit and a Thieme item; "northern gannet flicker fusion" returned the critical-fusion-frequency review, Wikipedia, a McGill species page and gannet species pages, with no gannet flicker value. "Morus spectral sensitivity" returned general spectral-sensitivity pages and a rodent cone paper; "northern gannet spectral sensitivity" returned Wikipedia, a paper on sexual plumage dichromatism in a size-monomorphic seabird (plumage colour seen through a bird visual model, which is not a pigment measurement) and species pages. "Sulidae vision review" returned Karger's "Spectral Transmittance of the Ocular Media of" (Brain Behavior and Evolution, 10.1159/000551766, title cut off in the result), which may give a gannet or booby ocular-media band; it is a lead on the wanted list, so lambda_max_nm is not in this record (main already holds Morus serrator ocular-media rows from sweep-6 and recheck-5-fixed, and sws1_type rows for both species from oa-2). Main holds no Morus row for acuity, fields, flicker or interreceptor angle. WebSearch returned result titles and links only, so web results were judged by title.
